name: Liquid cooling retrofit: CDU capacity is the ceiling on rack density in an existing building (LiquidStack CDU-1MW, up to 1.35 MW per row)
region: Global (manufacturing and service via Trane Technologies)
price_basis: No published price. CDU capacity is quoted per site after a density and cooling-architecture assessment; the vendor's own selector tool gates any number behind a sales conversation.
notes: RECORDED AS A SUPPLY CHANNEL BECAUSE WHEN YOU CANNOT BUILD A NEW DATAHALL, A CDU IS THE PRODUCT THAT DETERMINES WHAT FITS. LiquidStack publishes the density ceiling of its own hardware, which is the honest upper bound on a retrofit: CDU-1MW 'Supports rack densities up to 1.35MW per row, compatible with next-generation GPU platforms', quick-ship 'live in weeks', with 'In-row and perimeter configurations for new builds and retrofit environments' and 'third-party validated performance and global service through Trane Technologies'. The GigaModular CDU scales 'from initial deployment to multi-megawatt capacity without infrastructure redesign', with N+1/N+2 redundancy, dual-redundant communications, and a thermally important claim: 'Supports 45C return water for chillerless operation - optimized for hyperscale efficiency'. Chillerless operation matters because a colo whose whole strategy is air-cooled chillers (as Vantage's is) can be brought into direct-to-chip service by running the loop warm enough to reject heat without chillers, which is a cheaper retrofit than adding a chiller plant. TREAT THE DENSITY NUMBERS AS VENDOR-MARKETING CAPABILITY CLAIMS, not measured deployments: 'up to 1.35MW per row' is a per-ROW figure across multiple racks, not a per-rack figure, and it is ~11x the 120 kW of a GB200 NVL72 rack, so it is a headroom statement about the CDU class rather than a claim about any specific rack. The vendor names NVIDIA Vera Rubin as a supported platform - the rack-scale generation AFTER the parts in this repo - so treat current-generation fit as inferred from 'next-generation GPU platforms' rather than certified per SKU. The strategic read: CDU vendors are the ones telling you the industry has decided the transition is to liquid, and that the binding constraint on a retrofit is the coolant-distribution hardware, not the server.
